Ege: Turkish, 'Aegean' (Ege Denizi), also used as a given name; the region name is of Greek origin.
Sumaya: Arabic, a variant of Sumayya, a diminutive of sumuw meaning 'elevation' or 'high status'. Sumayya was an early Muslim martyr.
Salsabil: Arabic, the name of a spring in Paradise mentioned in the Quran, meaning 'flowing, sweet water'.
Luiza: Portuguese, Polish and Romanian form of Louise, the French feminine of Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Judy: English pet form of Judith, from Hebrew Yehudit, 'woman of Judah' or 'praised'.
Félien: Probably a modern French variant of Félix or Félicien, from Latin felix, 'happy, fortunate'.
Aïden: Variant spelling of Aidan, from Irish Áedán, a diminutive of áed 'fire'.
Evin: Kurdish and Turkish, meaning 'love' or 'beloved'. Possibly also a variant of Irish Evin; origin varies by use.
Rawan: Arabic, meaning 'flowing, gently moving' or 'the one who quenches thirst'; also used in Kurdish.
Léonor: French and Spanish form of Eleanor, of uncertain origin, perhaps Provençal Aliénor; often linked to Latin leo 'lion' by folk association.
Zéphyr: French, from Greek Zephyros, the west wind. Used for a gentle breeze.
Noyan: Turkish, from Mongolian noyan, an old title meaning 'lord' or 'commander'.
Eleanore: Variant spelling of Eleanor, of uncertain origin; possibly Provençal Aliénor, or a form of Helen meaning 'torch' or 'light'.
Jackson: English surname meaning 'son of Jack', Jack being a pet form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Theodora: Greek, from theos 'god' and doron 'gift', meaning 'gift of God'. Feminine of Theodore.
Éléa: Probably a modern French coined name, perhaps from Greek helios 'sun' or a variant of Éléa/Elea, an ancient Greek city.
Mélya: Modern French invented name, probably blending Mélissa or Amélie with the ending -ya.
Yliano: Modern coined name, probably a variant of Italian Iliano or Giuliano. Origin uncertain.
Ramatoulaye: West African (Wolof, Fula), from Arabic Rahmat Allah, 'mercy of God'.
Islem: Maghrebi spelling of Arabic Islam, meaning 'submission' to God, and by extension 'peace'.
Laia: Catalan short form of Eulàlia, from Greek eulalos, 'well-spoken'. Saint Eulalia is Barcelona's patron.
Tilio: Probably a modern variant of Italian Attilio or Tilo, from Latin Attilius, a Roman family name. Origin uncertain.
Alyna: Probably a variant of Alina, itself a short form of names like Adelina, or Slavic Alina; origin uncertain.
Hera: Greek, the queen of the gods in Greek mythology; the meaning is uncertain, possibly 'protectress'.
Siméo: Probably a French variant of Siméon (Simeon), from Hebrew Shim'on, 'he has heard'.
Abdulrahman: Arabic, 'servant of the Merciful' (ar-Rahman), one of the names of God.
Melya: Modern coined name, probably from Mélia or Amélie, or Melia from Greek meaning 'ash tree' nymph. Origin uncertain.
Araz: Turkish and Azeri, from the Aras River in the Caucasus. Also a Persian name meaning 'cheerful'.
Kenayah: Modern coined name, probably an elaboration of Kenya or Kenna. Origin uncertain.
Álvaro: Spanish and Portuguese, probably from Germanic alwar, 'all-wary' or 'guardian of all'.
Leone: Italian, from Latin leo, 'lion'. Also a Germanic-influenced form of Leo.
Zein: Arabic, meaning 'beauty, grace'. Also spelled Zain.
Ezyo: Modern coined name, probably a variant of Ezio, Italian, perhaps from Greek Aetios 'eagle'. Origin uncertain.
Adria: Latin, 'from Hadria' (the Adriatic region), or a feminine form of Adrian. Also used in Catalan.
Cézaar: Dutch spelling of Caesar, a Roman family name of uncertain origin, later understood as 'emperor'.
Riven: Modern English invented name, perhaps from the word 'riven' meaning 'split'. Origin uncertain.
Roo: English pet form of names such as Ruth, Rupert or Kangaroo; also a modern nickname-name. Origin uncertain.
Amari: African-American coinage, probably from Arabic or Igbo; often said to mean 'strength' or 'eternal'. Origin uncertain.
Matvii: Ukrainian (Matviy), a form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Emiliia: Ukrainian transliteration of Emilia, the feminine of Latin Aemilius, 'rival' or 'eager'.
Emre: Turkish, from the Turkish word for 'friend' or 'lover', linked to the poet Yunus Emre.
Sebastiaan: Dutch form of Sebastian, from Greek Sebastos, 'venerable' or 'revered', originally 'from Sebaste'.
Klaas: Dutch short form of Nicolaas, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Sanne: Dutch short form of Susanna, from Hebrew shoshannah, 'lily'.
Frederik: Dutch and Scandinavian form of Frederick, from Germanic 'peaceful ruler'.
Laora: Probably a variant of Laura, from Latin laurus, 'laurel'. Origin uncertain.
Lene: Scandinavian and German short form of Helene, from Greek 'torch' or 'bright'. Also short for Magdalene.
Abdellah: Maghrebi spelling of Arabic Abdullah, 'servant of God'.
Cameron: Scottish, from the clan name Cameron, from Gaelic cam-sron, 'crooked nose'.
Tony: Short form of Anthony, from the Roman family name Antonius, of uncertain origin.
Isaura: Latin, 'woman from Isauria', a region of Asia Minor. Popular in Portuguese and Spanish.
Corneel: Dutch form of Cornelius, from Latin cornu 'horn', or a Roman family name.
Bastian: German short form of Sebastian, from Greek Sebastos, 'venerable'.
Celina: Variant of Selina or Celine, from Latin caelum 'heaven', or from Greek Selene, 'moon'.
Safwane: French transliteration of Arabic Safwan, meaning 'clear, pure' or 'smooth rock'.
Mathiz: Modern variant of Mathis, a short form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Siem: Dutch short form of Simon or Siemen, from Hebrew 'he has heard'.
Inés: Spanish form of Agnes, from Greek hagne, 'pure, holy'.
Moïra: From Irish Máire, a form of Mary; also Greek moira, 'fate', as in the Moirai.
Doha: Arabic, meaning 'forenoon' or 'late morning light'; also the capital of Qatar.
Eunice: Greek, from eu 'good' and nike 'victory', meaning 'good victory'. Biblical mother of Timothy.
Aïda: Arabic, meaning 'visitor' or 'returning'; also the title heroine of Verdi's opera.
Zana: Albanian and Slavic, meaning 'fairy' or 'nymph'. Also a Persian form with other senses.
Andréas: French and Greek form of Andrew, from Greek andreios, 'manly, brave'.
Musab: Arabic, Mus'ab, meaning 'young camel'. Mus'ab ibn Umayr was an early companion of Muhammad.
Raul: Spanish, Portuguese and French form of Ralph, from Germanic 'wolf counsel'.
Tymon: Polish form of Timon, from Greek 'honour'. Also used for Timothy.
Lylia: Probably a variant of Lilia or Lilya, from Latin lilium, 'lily'. Also used as Arabic-influenced Leila, 'night'.
Oliwier: Polish form of Oliver, probably from Old French olivier 'olive tree', or Germanic 'elf army'.
Lucian: From Latin Lucianus, derived from Lucius, from lux 'light'.
Alaric: Germanic, from ala 'all' and ric 'ruler', 'ruler of all'. The Visigoth king who sacked Rome.
Gianna: Italian short form of Giovanna, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Awa: West African (Wolof, Fula), a form of Eve; also Japanese and Hawaiian meanings in other contexts.
Phéline: Probably a French coined name, perhaps from Latin felis 'cat' or a variant of Féline. Origin uncertain.
Elikya: Lingala, meaning 'hope', used in Congolese families.
Masha: Russian pet form of Maria, from Hebrew Miryam, of uncertain meaning.
Adela: Germanic, from adal, 'noble'. Also used in Spanish and Slavic languages.
Castor: Greek Kastor, one of the Dioscuri twins; possibly 'beaver' in Latin or 'to excel' in Greek.
Gustaaf: Dutch form of Gustav, from Old Norse or Germanic, perhaps 'staff of the Goths'.
Iosua: Romanian and Latin form of Joshua, from Hebrew Yehoshua, 'God is salvation'.
Vie: French and Dutch for 'life'; as a name probably a short form of Violet or similar. Origin uncertain.
Fanta: West African (Mandinka, Fula) female name; also a soft drink brand. Meaning varies.
Edoardo: Italian form of Edward, from Old English ead 'wealth' and weard 'guardian'.
Matías: Spanish form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Marcelle: French feminine of Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, a diminutive of Marcus, probably from Mars.
Nellie: English pet form of Helen, Eleanor or Ellen; Helen means 'torch' or 'bright one'.
Zeynab: Arabic, Zaynab, from a fragrant tree or from zayn 'adornment' of the father. Daughter of Muhammad.
Elon: Hebrew, 'oak tree'. A biblical name; also used in Hebrew and as a modern given name.
Matia: Italian and Georgian variant of Mattia, from Matthias, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Azzurra: Italian, meaning 'sky blue', from Arabic lazaward via Persian.
Élodie: French, probably from Visigothic Alodia, meaning 'foreign riches', or from Greek helodes.
Soujoud: Arabic, Sujud, meaning 'prostration' in prayer; used as a girls' name in the Maghreb.
Ariella: Hebrew, 'lioness of God', feminine of Ariel. Also Italian use.
Louwie: Dutch pet form of Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Rare: Probably a modern coined name or nickname, perhaps from the English word 'rare'. Origin uncertain.
Isayah: Variant of Isaiah, from Hebrew Yeshayahu, 'God is salvation'.
Boas: Hebrew Boaz, a biblical figure, probably meaning 'in him is strength'. Dutch form.
Éléanore: French spelling of Eleanor, of uncertain origin, perhaps Provençal Aliénor or a form of Helen.
Maëlo: Breton, a form of Maël, from 'prince' or 'chief'. Possibly modern coined variant.
Bobbie: English pet form of Robert, from Germanic 'bright fame'. Used for both sexes.
Elaya: Probably a modern coinage, perhaps from Hebrew El 'God' or a variant of Eliyah. Origin uncertain.
Ève: French form of Eve, from Hebrew Chavah, 'life' or 'living'.
Nazar: Arabic and Persian, 'sight' or 'glance'; also the Ukrainian form of Nazarius, 'from Nazareth'.
Eleanora: Latinised form of Eleanor, of uncertain origin; possibly Provençal Aliénor or a form of Helen.
Hélios: Greek, 'sun'. Helios was the Greek sun god.
Trim: Albanian, meaning 'brave, hero'. Also an English word. Used as a boys' name in Kosovo and Albania.
Makar: Russian and Ukrainian form of Makarios, from Greek makarios, 'blessed, happy'.
Umi: Japanese, 'sea' (also 'ocean'). Also used in Swahili and Arabic with other meanings.
Marine: French, from Latin marinus, 'of the sea'. Feminine of Marin.
Fanny: English and French pet form of Frances (Françoise), 'free one' or 'from France'.
Mélissa: Greek melissa, 'honey bee'. Melissa was a nymph in Greek mythology.
Yann: Breton and French form of Jean (John), from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Melanie: Greek melania, 'black' or 'dark'. Saint Melania was a Roman noblewoman.
Catherine: French and English, from Greek Aikaterine, of uncertain origin, later linked to katharos 'pure'.
Mattias: Scandinavian and Dutch form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Fee: German pet form of Felicitas or Sophie; also 'fairy' (Fee in French and German).
Tuana: Probably a variant of Turkish Tuğana or Tuna, the Turkish name of the Danube. Origin uncertain.
Kerim: Turkish and Bosnian form of Arabic Karim, 'generous, noble'.
Thibau: Variant of Thibaut, French form of Theobald, Germanic 'bold people'.
Witse: Frisian, a short form of Witze or Wietse, from Germanic wit 'wise' or 'white'. Origin uncertain.
Junior: English, from Latin iunior, 'younger'. Used for a son named after his father.
Jasmin: Persian yasmin, 'jasmine flower', through Arabic and French.
Lyse: French pet form of Élise or Lise, from Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Leny: Probably a pet form of Leonard, Lena or Leon, or a variant of Lenny. Origin uncertain.
Cristiano: Italian and Portuguese form of Christian, from Latin christianus, 'follower of Christ'.
Jaan: Estonian form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. Also Arabic and Hindi, 'life, soul'.
Elouan: Breton, Elouan, possibly from Breton 'light' or a form of Alan. Origin uncertain.
Yamina: Arabic, Yamina, 'right hand' and hence 'blessed, fortunate', from yamin.
Noemi: Italian and Spanish form of Naomi, from Hebrew 'pleasantness'.
Adélaïde: French form of Adelaide, from Germanic adal 'noble' and heid 'kind', 'noble kind'.
Lisanne: Dutch blend of Lisa and Anne; Lisa is from Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'; Anne from 'grace'.
Ivana: Slavic feminine of Ivan, a form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Maithé: Probably a French variant of Maïté, a Basque form of Marie. Origin uncertain.
Benyamin: Persian, Arabic and Turkish form of Benjamin, Hebrew 'son of the right hand'.
Léontine: French, from Latin leo 'lion'; feminine of Léonce.
Florien: Variant of Florian, from Latin florus, 'flowering, blooming'.
Salmane: French spelling of Arabic Salman, from salm 'peace' or 'safe'. Companion of Muhammad.
Nathanael: Hebrew, 'God has given'. A biblical disciple.
Walter: Germanic, from wald 'rule' and heri 'army', 'army ruler'.
Chaya: Hebrew, 'life' or 'alive'. Also Sanskrit 'shadow' in India.
Taylor: English occupational surname from Old French tailleur, 'tailor'.
Simay: Turkish, from Persian simay, 'face, appearance, countenance'.
Layna: Probably a variant of Lena, Elena or Layla. Origin uncertain.
Vittorio: Italian form of Victor, from Latin victor, 'conqueror'.
Eloan: Probably a Breton variant of Elouan or Alan. Origin uncertain.
Emmie: English pet form of Emma, Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Sören: Scandinavian and German form of Søren, from Latin severus, 'stern, strict'.
Arina: Russian form of Irene, from Greek eirene, 'peace'.
Kadija: Variant of Arabic Khadija, 'premature child' or 'early baby'. First wife of Muhammad.
Tudor: Romanian form of Theodore, from Greek 'gift of God'. Also the English dynasty from Welsh Tudur.
Théodora: French form of Theodora, Greek 'gift of God'.
Hania: Arabic Hania, 'happy, pleased'; also a Polish pet form of Anna.
Ayhan: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and han 'ruler', 'lord of the moon'.
Matin: Persian, meaning 'firm, steadfast, strong'. Also French for 'morning'.
Abrar: Arabic, plural of barr, 'the righteous, pious'.
Elohim: Hebrew, 'God', the plural form used for the God of Israel in the Bible. Rare as a given name.
Elyan: Probably a modern variant of Elian or Elouan, with possible Welsh or Breton roots. Origin uncertain.
Lilie: Variant of Lily, from the flower, Latin lilium.
Eliel: Hebrew, 'my God is God'. Biblical name.
Noeh: Variant spelling of Noah, Hebrew 'rest' or 'comfort'.
Gaby: Pet form of Gabriel or Gabrielle, Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Aryana: Persian and Sanskrit, 'noble' or 'of the Aryans'; also a variant of Ariana.
Sira: Probably Spanish or Catalan, or from Hebrew Sirah; also Turkish and Arabic usage. Origin uncertain.
Ayham: Arabic, a form of Ayham, perhaps meaning 'brave' or related to 'confusing'. Origin uncertain.
Eliyah: Variant of Elijah, Hebrew Eliyahu, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Minte: Frisian and Dutch, a short form of names with 'mint' or Germanic 'memory, love'. Origin uncertain.
Dot: English pet form of Dorothy, from Greek 'gift of God'.
Josiah: Hebrew Yoshiyahu, 'Yahweh supports' or 'healed by Yahweh'. A biblical king.
Assiyah: Arabic Asiya, 'one who heals' or 'comforter'. Name of the Pharaoh's wife in Islamic tradition.
Ayra: Probably Arabic or Turkish, meaning 'honourable' or a variant of Aira. Origin uncertain.
Qays: Arabic, meaning 'firmness, strength'. Also a historic Arab tribe.
River: English nature name, from the word river, from Latin ripa 'bank'.
Asiyah: Arabic, 'one who heals' or 'comforter'. Name of the Pharaoh's wife in Islamic tradition.
Mace: English, from a medieval nickname or from Old French masse 'club'. Also a form of Mathias.
Adar: Hebrew, a month name; also Hebrew 'noble' and Irish 'father'. Origin varies.
Naëlya: Modern French coinage, probably a variant of Nelia or Naélia. Origin uncertain.
Rital: Probably a modern variant of Ritalin or a coined name; origin uncertain.
Nusaybah: Arabic, Nusayba, a diminutive; Nusayba bint Ka'b was an early female Muslim warrior.
Mélio: Modern French coinage, probably from Mélo or Emilio. Origin uncertain.
Asinat: Possibly a variant of Egyptian Asenath, 'belonging to Neith', the wife of Joseph. Origin uncertain.
Marsel: Variant of Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, a diminutive of Marcus.
Maloé: Breton-French coinage, probably from Malo (Saint Malo) with Chloé or Noé. Origin uncertain.
Mathéïs: Modern French variant of Mathis, from Matthias, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
